interest: This document offers a concise window into U.S. State Department monitoring and administrative indexing of foreign property rights in Imperial Japan during the interwar period. Although only the purport sheet survives in this file, it references the legal status of alien landholders under Japan's Alien Land Law of November 10, 1926, showing U.S. diplomatic interest in reciprocal property ownership and foreign legal standing in Japan as bilateral relations grew increasingly strained in 1938.
overview: This file consists of a single Department of State record sheet (purport card) for decimal classification 894.5200, which covers the rights of foreign nationals to hold or acquire real property in Japan. The entry, recorded on April 25, 1938, indexes document 894.5200/1 prepared by Joseph W. Ballantine of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs (FE) for F2. The summary outlines the provisions of Japan's Alien Land Law of November 10, 1926, which granted foreign nationals the right to own real property on an equal footing with Japanese subjects, subject to certain qualifications and reciprocal conditions.

subfiles.about: A State Department purport sheet summarizing a report on the legal rights of aliens to acquire and own land in Japan under the Alien Land Law of 1926.
subfiles.summary: This record sheet indexes document 894.5200/1, received on April 25, 1938, from Joseph W. Ballantine of the State Department's Division of Far Eastern Affairs addressed to F2. It summarizes the provisions of the Alien Land Law of Japan enacted on November 10, 1926. According to the purport, the statute allowed aliens to own real property on an equal footing with Japanese nationals, though subject to certain qualifications.
